subject: SLA packaging and buydown offer for BrightBridge
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@brightbridge.com>, Tom Chan <tom@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA packaging and buydown offer for BrightBridge

Hi Elaine/Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a concise packaging note with three availability tiers and the associated response windows and credit schedules (SLA_Tiers_20260903.pdf). High level ask: BrightBridge had indicated wanting predictable cost and a meaningful concession for a 12–24m committed spend. We sketched two ways to do that:

1) Tiered availability + credits (pay-as-you-go with SLA credits when we miss the SLO) — no long-term commit.
2) Committed buydown (12/24 months) — we apply a one-time buydown discount to the premium SLA band and include a modest on-call retainer for guaranteed escalation coverage.

Specific points for your review:
- Uptime bands: 99.90% (standard), 99.95% (premium), 99.99% (mission-critical).
- Response windows: Premium = 1 hour P1, 4 hours P2; Mission-critical = 30 min P1, 2 hours P2.
- Failure credits: linear slab tied to monthly availability percentage (attached).
- Commit buydown: 12m = 12% off premium SLA over list; 24m = 18% off. These discounts require a minimum monthly committed spend (we list two commit tiers).

Before I loop legal, can you confirm the following so we tailor the counter:
- Which uptime band are you targeting for production?
- Do you prefer commit-based buydown or pay-as-you-go crediting?
- Any special regional failover / standby engineers requirement?

I'll hold a short internal alignment with Kim and Priyom before we send the formal counter.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Elaine Park <elaine@brightbridge.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Tom Chan <tom@brightbridge.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA packaging and buydown offer for BrightBridge

Rishi —

Appreciate the clear note and the tiers. A few answers up front:
- Target production requirement: 99.95% premium band for our analytics ingestion and low-latency scoring path.
- Preference: we prefer a commit model if the economics are meaningful — we want predictability for budgeting.
- Regional failover: must support automatic failover to our EU region with a 30-minute RTO for critical scoring endpoints.

On discounts: the team is looking for something closer to a 20–25% buydown on the premium SLA if we sign a 24-month commit (we run high volume, so we believe the consumption justify it). We also want to cap liability on credits to avoid double-counting during planned maintenance windows.

Can you provide a concrete counter with the 24m band and an explicit clause for planned maintenance carve-outs + an escalation roster with guaranteed names/roles? If you can give a working Doc with line items we can share with procurement and legal, that would speed things up.

Thanks —
Elaine Park
Head of Infrastructure, BrightBridge Analytics
elaine@brightbridge.com
+1 (617) 555-9987
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@brightbridge.com>, Tom Chan <tom@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SLA packaging and buydown offer for BrightBridge

Elaine —

Thanks for the specifics. We talked internally and prepared a concise counter. Summary below — full line-item counter attached (Counterproposal_BrightBridge_20260908.docx).

Counter summary (24m commit):
- Target band: 99.95% (Premium) for scoring/ingestion.
- Buydown: 20% off premium SLA list price applied as a monthly coupon for 24 months. We can stretch to 22% with an additional 10% annualized usage commit above the minimum tier.
- Liability cap: Credits limited to monthly subscription fee for the affected service; planned maintenance windows (up to 4 hrs monthly scheduled maintenance per region) are excluded from crediting. Emergency maintenance will be treated case-by-case.
- Regional failover: Included. We guarantee cross-region warm standby; RTO for scoring endpoints <= 30 minutes for mission-critical paths. Extra egress bandwidth in the event of failover is billable at marginal cost (we list a not-to-exceed rate).
- Escalation: weekly on-call rotation + named escalation engineers for first 12 months; will provide roster and contact card as an appendix in the Doc.
- Doc/Contract: we prepared a marked counter and uploaded to DocuSign for review (link below). Once BrightBridge signals approval in principle, we'll loop in Legal to finalize redlines.

Attached: Counterproposal_BrightBridge_20260908.docx (8 pages) — includes a) price table, b) credit matrix, c) maintenance carve-outs, d) named on-call roster template.

Request: if you can confirm acceptance of the 20–22% band (22% requires the incremental usage commit), we'll get legal to start a redline and I can send a pre-filled DocuSign for signatures.

Best —
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

Appreciate the counter and the clarity. BrightBridge is happy to proceed in principle with the 22% buydown conditional on the incremental usage commit (we'll confirm the numbers from procurement by EOD Monday). Two quick asks from legal:

1) Please provide a redline-ready MS Word of the counter (not PDF) with the maintenance carve-outs explicitly called out as a separate clause.
2) We need the named escalation roster (even a template with role + primary/secondary contact) included in the bundle to satisfy our SOC review.

If you can get the redline and roster in the next 48 hours we'll have procurement + legal begin parallel review. Once we pass that step we'll route to execs for signature.
